title: How do we write an expression for a situation and find its terms?
description: Coins of two princesses, metro tickets and the height of a window are each written as an expression, split into terms and worked out. The video checks each value by taking one term away.
teaching_notes: One idea: read the situation one piece at a time and write one term for each piece. A group of equal groups stays one term, so a bracket may sit inside it.

video_script.why: The child reads a situation, writes one term for each piece, names the terms and works out the value, as in the dosa example.
video_script.substitution: Change the amounts and the number of people and the method stays the same: one term for each kind of piece.
video_script.anchor: three situations in a column: two princesses with a queen's coins, metro tickets, and a window with border, grills and gaps
video_script.payoff_line: One term for each piece, then work out and add.

final_answer.spoken: two hundred and fifty coins, two hundred and twenty rupees, two hundred and forty rupees, and fifty three centimetres

maths_rules: coins: one princess doubles her 100, so 2 x 100 = 200; the other keeps half of 100, so 100 / 2 = 50; expression 2 x 100 + 100 / 2, terms 2 x 100 and 100 / 2, value 200 + 50 = 250
tickets for four adults and three children: 4 x 40 + 3 x 20 = 160 + 60 = 220; terms 4 x 40 and 3 x 20
tickets for two groups of three adults: 2 x (3 x 40) = 2 x 120 = 240; one term
window: two borders, six grills, seven gaps: 7 x 5 + 6 x 2 + 2 x 3 = 35 + 12 + 6 = 53 cm; terms 7 x 5, 6 x 2, 2 x 3
video_script.design: One idea: one term for each piece of the situation, then work out and add. The three situations stay in the anchor band; the working band shows the expression, the terms and the value. No hard clear.
open_questions: The window picture is not in the extracted text. The counts of six grills, seven gaps and two borders come from the worklist and are consistent with a gap on each side of every grill.

<bookmark mark='m2'/>An adult ticket costs forty rupees, and a child ticket costs twenty.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The window has borders of three, grills of two, and gaps of five centimetres.

marks.m1: 2 × 100 is written for the doubled coins

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, one princess doubled her coins, which is two times one hundred.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The other has half of one hundred, which is one hundred divided by two.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The terms are two times one hundred, and one hundred divided by two.
The value is two hundred plus fifty.

marks.m1: 4 × 40 + 3 × 20 is written and its two terms are boxed
marks.m4: the bracket is worked out first: 3 × 40 = 120, so 2 × 120

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, four adults and three children cost four times forty plus three times twenty.
The terms are four times forty, and three times twenty.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>That is one hundred and sixty plus sixty.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Two groups of three adults is two times the bracket three times forty, which is one term.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The bracket is one hundred and twenty, so we get two times one hundred and twenty.

marks.m1: 7 × 5 is written for the seven gaps
marks.m2: 6 × 2 is written for the six grills and 2 × 3 for the two borders
marks.m3: the three terms are boxed and worked out: 35 + 12 + 6

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, the window has seven gaps of five, which is seven times five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>It has six grills of two, and two borders of three.
The terms are seven times five, six times two, and two times three.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The value is thirty five plus twelve plus six.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check each total by taking one term away.
Taking fifty away from the coins leaves two times one hundred.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Taking sixty away from the tickets leaves four times forty.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Six adults at forty rupees each cost the same as two groups of three.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Taking six away from the height leaves thirty five plus twelve.

marks.m2: the units coins, rupees and cm are underlined

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>One term for each piece, then work out and add.
The princesses have two hundred and fifty coins together.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The tickets cost two hundred and twenty rupees, and two hundred and forty rupees.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The window is fifty three centimetres high.
